findings.title: A backup code can be used without verifying the password
findings.body: The password check above is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty. The new backup-code branch then accepts a valid `backupCode` without validating that TOTP value at all. A caller can therefore post a valid backup code plus any arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` to the credentials callback and authenticate without supplying the account password (and can also bypass the external-identity gate, which uses the same `!credentials.totpCode` condition). Backup codes are presented as a replacement for the authenticator, not for the primary login factor. Verify the primary factor independently of the presence of either second-factor field, or bind the first-factor verification to a server-side challenge.

findings.title: Backup-code redemption is not atomic, so one code can authorize concurrent logins
findings.body: Each request reads and validates the encrypted backup-code array, then separately writes an array with the matched entry replaced by `null`. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both read the original array, both pass `indexOf`, and both return an authenticated user before either write is observed. This violates the stated one-time-use guarantee and lets a stolen code be redeemed more than once. Consume the code with a transaction or a conditional update tied to the originally-read stored value, and reject the request when that update affects no row.

findings.title: External-provider 2FA users have no backup-code recovery path
findings.body: When `totpEmail` is set, which is the post-Google/SAML external 2FA flow, the page selects `ExternalTotpFooter` rather than `TwoFactorFooter`. That footer only provides Cancel, so it never sets `twoFactorLostAccess`; consequently the `BackupCode` component at line 221 can never be rendered. Users already routed through this external TOTP flow cannot use backup codes after losing their authenticator, despite this feature adding backup-code login.

findings.title: The enable-modal password visibility toggle cannot reveal the password
findings.body: `PasswordField` sets its dynamic `type` before spreading props, so the explicit `type="password"` passed here overwrites it on every render. Clicking the eye button changes its icon/state but the underlying input remains a password input. Omit this prop at this call site or make `PasswordField` spread props before applying its controlled `type`.

findings.title: The show-password control was removed from keyboard tab navigation
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` makes the interactive show/hide password button unreachable using normal keyboard navigation. This regresses keyboard-only users' ability to use the password visibility feature across every `PasswordField`, including the newly changed 2FA setup field. Keep the button focusable or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible control.

findings.title: The recovery authentication behavior is not covered by tests
findings.body: The new test coverage only checks that a download has the expected filename and that clicking Copy shows a toast; it explicitly leaves backup-code login and disabling with a backup code as TODOs. It never verifies that a generated code authenticates, an invalid code is rejected, or a redeemed code cannot be reused. As a result, the central security behavior of this feature, including the one-time-use invariant, can regress without test detection.
